question: What is the main goal of the whole operating theatre team?

options.A: Ensuring safe and coordinated patient care during surgery
options.B: Training new medical students in advanced surgical skills
options.C: Cleaning and disinfecting the theatre after every procedure
options.D: Maintaining hospital financial records and surgical supplies

explanation: Great job thinking about teamwork! Everyone in the theatre works hand-in-hand to keep the patient safe and make sure the surgery goes smoothly. You've got this! [learn more](GNS123_U5_T13#GNS123_U5_T13_h1)

question: Which member of the theatre team is part of the sterile team?
explanation: The scrub nurse scrubs up, wears sterile gear, and handles sterile instruments right beside the surgeon. Think 'sterile zone, scrub nurse!' [learn more](GNS123_U5_T13#GNS123_U5_T13_h1)

question: Who takes ultimate responsibility for the surgical procedure?
explanation: The surgeon leads the team and carries the main legal and clinical responsibility for how the surgery goes. Every team member has a vital role, but the lead surgeon guides the ship! [learn more](GNS123_U5_T13#GNS123_U5_T13_h2)

question: A surgical assistant holds tissue away so the surgeon can see clearly. What is this called?
explanation: When assistants hold back organs or tissues to give a clear view, it's called 'retracting.' Picture holding curtains open wide so you can see inside! [learn more](GNS123_U5_T13#GNS123_U5_T13_h2)

question: What is the main duty of the anaesthetist during an operation?

options.A: Monitoring the patient's vital signs and managing pain
options.B: Transporting the patient safely from the ward to theatre
options.C: Documenting sponge and instrument counts every thirty minutes
options.D: Handing sterile instruments directly to the operating surgeon

explanation: The anaesthetist focuses entirely on keeping the patient asleep, stable, and pain-free while watching all life signs closely. They are the patient's guardian angels for comfort! [learn more](GNS123_U5_T13#GNS123_U5_T13_h3)

question: Why does the anaesthetist stay close to the patient's head during surgery?

options.A: To assist the surgeon with knot-tying and tissue retraction
options.B: To manage the airway and monitor breathing continuously
options.C: To clean blood off the surgical instruments during the operation
options.D: To count surgical instruments before the wound is closed

explanation: By staying right by the head, the anaesthetist can easily keep the airway open, give oxygen, and watch vital signs every second. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T13#GNS123_U5_T13_h3)

question: Where does the scrub nurse position themselves during an operation?

options.B: Outside the sterile zone managing room records
options.C: In the recovery ward receiving incoming patients
options.D: At the patient's head near the anaesthetic machine

explanation: The scrub nurse wears sterile personal protective gear and stands right inside the sterile zone, ready to pass tools to the surgeon. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T13#GNS123_U5_T13_h4)

question: What critical safety check is shared between the scrub nurse and the circulating nurse?

options.A: Obtaining written consent from the patient

explanation: Safety first! Both nurses double-check and count everything used so nothing gets accidentally left behind inside the patient. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T13#GNS123_U5_T13_h4)

question: Which task is usually handled by the circulating nurse?

options.A: Scrubbing up and handing instruments to the surgeon
options.B: Performing the actual surgical incision on the patient
options.C: Managing the patient's airway and breathing tubes
options.D: Opening sterile packages and managing room equipment

explanation: The circulating nurse is unsterile and moves freely around the room to open supplies, manage equipment, and help the team with whatever they need. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T13#GNS123_U5_T13_h5)

question: Why is the circulating nurse considered the patient's voice in the theatre?

options.A: Because the patient is unconscious and unable to speak for themselves
options.B: Because this nurse holds the legal license to perform surgery
options.C: Because this nurse decides what type of anaesthesia to give
options.D: Because this nurse stays inside the sterile zone at all times

explanation: Since the patient is asleep under anaesthesia, the circulating nurse acts as their advocate, watching out for their safety and comfort the whole time. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T13#GNS123_U5_T13_h5)

question: What is a major duty of the health orderly in the operating theatre?

options.A: Counting surgical needles before wound closure
options.B: Scrubbing in to assist the surgeon at the table
options.D: Transporting patients and heavy supplies safely

explanation: Health orderlies are essential for smooth operations—they handle patient transport, heavy lifting, waste disposal, and moving equipment. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T13#GNS123_U5_T13_h6)

question: How do health orderlies help control infections in the theatre?

options.A: They wear sterile gowns and handle surgical instruments
options.B: They scrub the surgeon's hands before the operation begins
options.C: They help clean the theatre and dispose of waste between cases
options.D: They sterilize surgical blades inside the autoclave machine

explanation: By clearing waste and cleaning up after procedures, orderlies play a huge part in keeping the theatre safe from hospital-acquired infections. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T13#GNS123_U5_T13_h6)

question: What is the main reason a nursing student is in the operating theatre?

options.B: To replace the scrub nurse during complex procedures
options.C: To act as the primary circulating nurse for major cases
options.D: To learn and observe surgical nursing care firsthand

explanation: As a student, you are there to gain experience, connect your classroom notes to real-life practice, and learn safely under supervision! [learn more](GNS123_U5_T13#GNS123_U5_T13_h7)

question: A nursing student in a sterile gown accidentally lets their hands drop below their waist. What should they do?

options.A: Step back one foot and continue assisting the surgeon
options.B: Continue working because the gown is still clean on top
options.C: Acknowledge that sterility is broken and get a new gown
options.D: Ask the circulating nurse to wipe the gloves with alcohol

explanation: In theatre rules, anything below the waist is considered unsterile. Don't worry—accidents happen! Just step back, re-gown, and keep learning. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T13#GNS123_U5_T13_h7)
